intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon-era royal palace while dressed in traditional Hanbok attire. Hanbok rental shops are located just outside the palace gates, making it easy to combine both activities. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry. Ideal for Day 2 or 3 after settling in, and best done in the morning to avoid crowds. Stay nearby in Jongno-gu to walk directly to the palace.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). The market is lively and authentic, offering a true local food experience without tourist markup. Book a guided food tour or explore independently. Stay in Jongno-gu or Euljiro for easy access.

experiences.name: Hongdae K-Culture & Street Performance Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-pop and youth culture hub. Hongdae is packed with indie music venues, K-pop dance studios offering drop-in classes, street performers, quirky cafes, and K-beauty shops. Join a K-pop dance class at a local studio for around $15–20, then explore the nightlife and street art. This area is best experienced in the late afternoon through evening when energy peaks.

experiences.name: Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Experience
experiences.description: Wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Visit Ssamziegil, an artsy courtyard mall with local designers and handmade goods. Stop at a traditional Korean tea house to try omija tea or sikhye. This culturally rich neighborhood is walkable from Gyeongbokgung and Gwangjang Market, making it perfect for a combined day out. Ideal for mid-trip exploration.

experiences.name: Korean BBQ Dinner Experience in Mapo-gu
experiences.description: Enjoy an authentic Korean BBQ dinner at a local grill restaurant in the Mapo-gu area near Hongdae or Hapjeong. Order samgyeopsal (pork belly) or galbi (beef short ribs), grilled tableside and wrapped in lettuce with ssamjang paste. Pair with unlimited banchan side dishes and soju or makgeolli. This is a quintessential Korean dining ritual best enjoyed with a group. Staying in Mapo-gu puts you steps away from top BBQ spots.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or bus to Bupyeong station. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip.

meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour GS25 or CU convenience store near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or hotteok (₩1,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you'll be tired from the flight. Buy your T-money card at the airport (₩4,000 deposit). Exchange some cash at the airport for better rates. Dress warmly; December temperatures hover around 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Enjoy the complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn if included. Explore the Bupyeong area on foot — visit Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center (Bupyeong Modoo Mall), one of Korea's largest underground malls, great for affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) to Incheon Chinatown — Korea's only Chinatown, just 2 stops away. Walk through the colorful murals and archways, then head to nearby Jayu Park (Freedom Park) for panoramic views of Incheon port. Explore the Open Port Area with its historic Japanese and Chinese colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinpo International Market (신포국제시장) in Incheon for street food and local eats. Try the famous Sinpo dak-gangjeong (sweet crispy chicken) and browse the stalls.

meals.lunch: Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) at a Chinatown restaurant — authentic and cheap (₩6,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Sinpo Market street food: dak-gangjeong, tteokbokki, sundae (₩5,000–8,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: All locations today are within Incheon and easily reachable by subway from Bupyeong. Wear layers — it will be cold. Sinpo Market is lively in the evening despite winter.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway from Bupyeong to Hongdae (Line 1 to Seoul, transfer to Line 2 — about 50 min, ₩1,500). Explore Hongdae's vibrant street art, indie shops, and K-culture scene. Visit the Hongdae Free Market area and browse affordable K-pop merchandise shops and vintage clothing stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area for more affordable shopping and street food. Then head to Gyeongui Line Forest Park (경의선숲길), a beautiful linear park perfect for a winter stroll. Visit the Yonsei University campus nearby for a classic Korean university atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the evening — the area comes alive at night with buskers, street performers, and K-culture energy. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for a quintessential Korean experience (₩10,000–15,000/hour per room).

meals.lunch: Tteokbokki and eomuk (fish cake) from Hongdae street stalls (₩4,000–6,000)
meals.dinner: Budae jjigae (army stew) at a local Sinchon restaurant — hearty and warming for winter (₩8,000–10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is the heart of K-culture and youth culture in Seoul. Keep an eye out for idol fan cafes and K-pop pop-up stores. Subway fare from Bupyeong to Hongdae is approximately ₩1,500 each way.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) — Seoul's grandest Joseon-era palace. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from one of the many rental shops near the palace entrance (₩10,000–15,000/2 hours) and get free entry to the palace while wearing it. Explore the palace grounds and Gyeonghoeru Pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을) — a stunning neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the narrow alleys and enjoy the contrast of old and new Seoul. Then visit Insadong (인사동) for traditional crafts, tea houses, and K-culture souvenirs at reasonable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil courtyard complex for indie shops and street food. Head to nearby Tapgol Park area for a quiet evening walk.

meals.lunch: Gimbap and doenjang jjigae at a local bunsik restaurant near Insadong (₩5,000–7,000)
meals.dinner: Samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a budget BBQ restaurant in Insadong or Jongno area — look for set menus (₩10,000–13,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace entry is ₩3,000 (free with hanbok). The palace is stunning in winter — check if there are special winter light events. Bukchon can be slippery in cold weather, so wear good shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. This is a must for local food lovers. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini kimbap), and yukhoe (beef tartare) for breakfast/brunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the free outdoor areas and any free exhibitions inside. Then visit Dongdaemun History & Culture Park for a glimpse of Seoul's ancient city walls.
day_by_day.evening: Dongdaemun is famous for its massive shopping malls that open late into the night. Browse Doota Mall, Migliore, or the outdoor Dongdaemun Market for affordable K-fashion. The area is especially lively on weekends.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok and mayak gimbap (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: More Gwangjang Market food or a nearby kalguksu (knife noodle) restaurant (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Street food around Dongdaemun — tteokbokki, hotteok, and eomuk (₩5,000–7,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is busiest on weekends — arrive early to beat the crowds. DDP often hosts free cultural events and exhibitions. Dongdaemun shopping malls stay open until 5 AM — great for night owls.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's most famous shopping and beauty district. Browse the countless K-beauty shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young) for affordable skincare and cosmetics. Many shops offer free samples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) via the free cable car or hiking trail. Enjoy panoramic views of Seoul in winter. Visit the famous love lock fence. Then explore the surrounding Namsan Park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for the famous street food market that sets up in the evening. This is one of the best street food experiences in Seoul. Try Korean corn dogs, tteokbokki, and hotteok.

meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja — famous for kalguksu and mandu dumplings, a Seoul institution (₩9,000–11,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food market — try 3–4 different items (₩8,000–12,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower cable car costs ₩9,000 round trip; the observation deck costs extra (₩16,000) but the views from the park are free. Myeongdong street food vendors typically set up around 5–6 PM. Olive Young is the best place for affordable K-beauty products.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). The Secret Garden requires a guided tour (₩8,000) and is especially beautiful in winter with snow-dusted pavilions. Book in advance or arrive early as spots are limited.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (익선동) — a trendy neighborhood of converted hanok houses turned into cafes, restaurants, and boutiques. More authentic and less touristy than Bukchon. Perfect for K-culture exploration and Instagram-worthy spots.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jongno 3-ga area for pojangmacha (street tent bars) — a classic Korean evening experience. Sit under a tent, order anju (bar snacks) like pajeon (green onion pancake) and makgeolli (rice wine) for a very local, budget-friendly evening.

meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong cafe lunch — many offer affordable set menus or Korean fusion dishes (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Pojangmacha in Jongno — makgeolli + pajeon + sundae (₩10,000–15,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Palace entry is ₩3,000; Secret Garden tour is ₩8,000 extra. Book the Secret Garden tour online in advance at the palace website. Ikseon-dong is very photogenic — great for K-culture content.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Itaewon and walk up to Haebangchon (HBC) — a multicultural neighborhood with a local, non-touristy vibe. Explore the hillside streets and independent cafes. Then visit the nearby Bogwangdong neighborhood for a glimpse of authentic Seoul residential life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Yongsan Electronics Market (용산전자상가) — one of Asia's largest electronics markets. Great for browsing K-tech, gaming gear, and electronics at competitive prices. Even if you don't buy, it's a fascinating cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Visit War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) — free entry and one of Seoul's most impressive museums covering Korean history and the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits are accessible even in the evening.

meals.lunch: Haebangchon local restaurant — try dosirak (Korean lunch box set) or kimchi jjigae (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Yongsan area — galbi-tang (short rib soup) at a local restaurant, warming for winter (₩9,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: War Memorial of Korea is free and open Tuesday–Sunday, 9:30 AM–6 PM. Yongsan Electronics Market is a great place to buy affordable Korean tech accessories. Haebangchon has a great mix of Korean and international culture.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World (롯데월드) in Jamsil — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks. Budget option: buy a day pass (₩54,000) or just explore the free Lotte World Mall and Magic Island outdoor area. Alternatively, visit the free Lotte World Folk Museum inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Seokchon Lake (석촌호수) adjacent to Lotte World — a beautiful lake park that's lovely even in winter. Then explore the Jamsil area and visit the COEX Mall underground shopping complex nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam (강남) for the evening — explore Garosu-gil (가로수길), a tree-lined street with boutiques, cafes, and restaurants. Window shop and enjoy the upscale but walkable neighborhood.

meals.lunch: COEX Mall food court — wide variety of Korean dishes at reasonable prices (₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Garosu-gil area — look for affordable Korean set meal restaurants or a cozy ramen shop (₩8,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: If skipping Lotte World rides, the mall and lake area are completely free. COEX Mall also has a famous underground library (Starfield Library) — free to visit and very photogenic. Gangnam subway station is on Line 2.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in central Seoul. Free entry. The temple is beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round and may have special winter decorations. A peaceful contrast to the busy city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — an elevated highway converted into a beautiful urban stream. Walk along the stream from Gwanghwamun toward Dongdaemun. In winter, there are often special light installations along the stream.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration! Head to Myeongdong or Hongdae for the festive atmosphere — streets are decorated, carolers perform, and the city feels magical. Many young Koreans celebrate Christmas Eve as a romantic holiday.

meals.lunch: Cheonggyecheon area — try a local gukbap (rice soup) restaurant for a warming winter meal (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — treat yourself to Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek) at a local chicken restaurant in Myeongdong or Hongdae (₩15,000–20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the busiest nights in Seoul — expect crowds in Myeongdong and Hongdae. Cheonggyecheon Stream often has a special winter light festival (Lantern Festival) — check current events. Jogyesa Temple is free and open daily.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁) — a lesser-known but beautiful palace that's free to enter and usually uncrowded. Then walk to the Seoul Museum of History (서울역사박물관) next door — also free and excellent for understanding Seoul's history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seodaemun Prison History Hall (서대문형무소역사관) — a powerful museum in a former Japanese colonial-era prison, important for understanding Korean independence history (₩3,000 entry). Then explore the surrounding Seodaemun area.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Noryangjin Fish Market (노량진수산시장) — one of Seoul's largest wholesale fish markets. Buy fresh seafood at the market stalls and have it prepared at the restaurants upstairs for a fraction of restaurant prices. A unique and memorable experience.

meals.lunch: Near Seodaemun — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant, perfect for cold weather (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Noryangjin Fish Market — buy fresh sashimi, crab, or shrimp and have it prepared upstairs (₩15,000–25,000 depending on selection)

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions are open on Christmas Day in Korea as it's a public holiday but celebrated differently than in the West. Noryangjin Fish Market is open 24 hours — the freshest seafood is in the early morning, but evening is fine too. Seodaemun Prison is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway. The fortress walls stretch 5.7 km and offer great winter walks with views of the city. Entry is ₩1,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Paldalmun Gate area and the traditional market nearby. Visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace (행궁) — the temporary palace used by King Jeongjo (₩1,500 entry). Walk the fortress walls for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Spend your last full evening exploring the Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for any last-minute souvenir shopping. Have a farewell Korean BBQ dinner near the hotel.

meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — Suwon is famous for this dish; look for affordable lunch sets near the fortress (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Korean BBQ near Bupyeong hotel — samgyeopsal or chadolbaegi (beef brisket) farewell dinner (₩12,000–15,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is easily reached from Bupyeong via subway (Line 1 to Suwon Station, about 45–60 min, ₩1,800). The fortress is beautiful in winter and rarely crowded. Suwon galbi is a regional specialty not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack and check out of Toyoko Inn. If time allows, grab a last Korean breakfast at a nearby bunsik restaurant: haejang-guk (hangover soup) or kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) — a classic Korean morning meal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX or airport bus from Bupyeong. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Korean snacks, cosmetics, or gifts (Choco Pie, Pepero, Korean seaweed, etc.).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Local bunsik restaurant near hotel — haejang-guk or gimbap (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience store (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: On the plane or airport restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Bupyeong to Incheon Airport takes approximately 40–60 minutes by AREX or bus. Keep your T-money card topped up for the airport journey. Pack any liquid K-beauty products in checked luggage. Korean duty-free snacks make great affordable gifts — Choco Pie multipacks, dried seaweed, and instant ramyeon are popular choices.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage. Take Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or limousine bus to Bupyeong area. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Grab a late-night snack near the hotel at a nearby convenience store (GS25 or CU) or a 24-hour pojangmacha (street food tent).

meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snacks: triangle kimbap, instant ramen, hotteok, or a nearby 24-hour Korean diner near Bupyeong station

day_by_day.notes: Arrive well-rested. Purchase a T-money card at the airport for easy transit use throughout the trip. Exchange some currency at the airport for convenience. Dress warmly — December temperatures average around 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. After a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, explore Bupyeong Modoo Mall (underground shopping mall connected to Bupyeong Station) — one of Korea's largest underground shopping complexes. Browse local fashion, accessories, and K-culture merchandise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Incheon Chinatown (30 min by subway) — Korea's only official Chinatown, blending Korean and Chinese culture. Walk through the colorful gates, explore Jayu Park (Freedom Park) with its panoramic harbor views, and visit the nearby Sinpo International Market for local street food and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong area. Explore the lively Bupyeong street food alley near the station for dinner. Stroll through the local night market atmosphere and pick up any essentials for the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby bakery (Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours) — coffee and pastries around ₩5,000–8,000
meals.lunch: Sinpo Market street food: jajangmyeon (black bean noodles), tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork), or steamed buns — around ₩8,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Bupyeong street food alley: tteokbokki, sundae, twigim (fried snacks), or a sit-down Korean BBQ restaurant — around ₩15,000–25,000

day_by_day.notes: Incheon Chinatown is walkable from Incheon Station (Line 1). Wear layers and comfortable walking shoes. Jayu Park is beautiful even in winter with city views.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to central Seoul (approx. 40–50 min by subway from Bupyeong). Start at Gyeongbokgung Palace — Seoul's grandest Joseon-era palace. Arrive early (opens 9:00 AM) to watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (10:00 AM and 14:00 PM). Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) near the palace entrance for free or discounted entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bukchon Hanok Village — a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Explore the winding alleyways, admire the architecture, and enjoy the contrast of old and new Seoul. Continue to Insadong for K-culture shopping: traditional crafts, calligraphy, tea sets, and K-pop merchandise.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil — an artsy open-air shopping complex with indie shops, galleries, and cafes. Enjoy dinner in the area before heading back to the hotel.

meals.lunch: Insadong traditional restaurant: bibimbap or doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) set meal — around ₩10,000–15,000
meals.dinner: Insadong or Anguk area: samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) at a traditional restaurant — around ₩15,000–20,000

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Hanbok rental shops near the palace charge around ₩10,000–20,000/hour. Bukchon can be crowded on weekends — be respectful of residents. Subway Line 3 (Orange) connects Bupyeong area via transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) — take the cable car up Namsan Mountain for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Attach a love lock on the fence (a popular K-culture tradition). The tower area opens around 10:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Namsan and head to Myeongdong — Seoul's most famous shopping and street food district. Browse Korean skincare brands (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), fashion stores, and international brands. Sample street food along the main pedestrian street.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Myeongdong for dinner. Visit명동교자 (Myeongdong Kyoja) — one of Seoul's most iconic noodle restaurants. Afterward, explore the area's vibrant nightlife atmosphere and do some K-beauty shopping.

meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food: Korean corn dogs, egg bread (gyeran-ppang), tteokbokki, grilled skewers — around ₩8,000–15,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja: kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) or mandu (dumplings) — around ₩10,000–14,000

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower cable car costs around ₩9,500 round trip. The tower observation deck costs extra (₩21,000). December evenings are very cold on Namsan — bring a warm hat and gloves. Myeongdong is extremely lively on Friday evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). This UNESCO World Heritage Site requires a guided tour for the Secret Garden (book in advance online). The palace grounds are stunning even in winter with bare trees and traditional architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the design exhibitions, K-fashion pop-up stores, and the surrounding Dongdaemun Market area. Browse the massive fabric and fashion wholesale markets.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Dongdaemun's famous night shopping scene — many stores open until 5:00 AM. Grab dinner at one of the many restaurants in the area and enjoy the illuminated DDP at night.

meals.lunch: Near Changdeokgung: traditional Korean set meal (한정식 hanjeongsik lite) or a local restaurant — around ₩12,000–18,000
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area: dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) or a Korean BBQ restaurant — around ₩15,000–22,000

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours are limited — book online at the Cultural Heritage Administration website. Tours are available in English. DDP exhibitions may have separate entry fees (₩5,000–10,000). Saturday is busy — arrive early at popular spots.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the epicenter of Korean youth culture, indie music, street art, and K-pop. Visit on a Sunday morning when the Hongdae Free Market (홍대 자유시장) may be operating (check seasonal schedule). Browse street art murals and quirky cafes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a K-pop themed café or experience in Hongdae — many idol-themed cafes and entertainment company flagship stores are in this area. Explore the SM Entertainment, JYP, or HYBE (Big Hit) nearby areas. Visit the LINE FRIENDS Store or character-themed shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinchon or Hapjeong for dinner. These areas are popular with young Koreans and offer great mid-range dining options. Enjoy the Sunday evening atmosphere of western Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae café culture: brunch at a trendy café — around ₩10,000–15,000
meals.lunch: Hongdae street food or a popular local restaurant: buldak (fire chicken) or ramyeon — around ₩8,000–13,000
meals.dinner: Sinchon or Hapjeong: galbi (grilled ribs) or samgyeopsal (pork belly BBQ) at a local restaurant — around ₩18,000–25,000

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is best experienced in the afternoon and evening when street performers appear. Many K-pop entertainment company buildings are nearby (HYBE is in Yongsan, a short taxi ride). Wear comfortable shoes for lots of walking.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway/bus). This UNESCO-listed fortress from the Joseon Dynasty is spectacular in winter. Walk along the fortress walls for panoramic views of Suwon city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (temporary royal palace) within the fortress grounds. Visit the Korean Folk Village nearby if time permits — a living museum of traditional Korean culture with performances and demonstrations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Incheon/Bupyeong area. Relax and enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel. This is a good evening to do laundry or rest mid-trip.

meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — a local specialty! Try it at a traditional restaurant near the fortress — around ₩20,000–30,000
meals.dinner: Near Bupyeong hotel: Korean sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) or doenjang jjigae at a local restaurant — around ₩10,000–15,000

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress entry is free. The fortress wall walk takes about 2–3 hours for the full circuit. Dress very warmly — the fortress walls are exposed to wind. Korean Folk Village entry is around ₩15,000–25,000.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Itaewon and the War Memorial of Korea — a powerful and free museum documenting Korean history from ancient times through the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and artillery. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon's multicultural neighborhood — browse international restaurants, vintage clothing stores, antique shops, and the famous Itaewon main street. Visit Leeum Samsung Museum of Art nearby for world-class Korean and international art (check opening hours).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Itaewon's diverse restaurant scene. This is a great opportunity to try international cuisine or upscale Korean dining. The area has a vibrant evening atmosphere.

meals.lunch: Itaewon: international cuisine (Thai, Indian, Mexican) or Korean fusion — around ₩12,000–18,000
meals.dinner: Itaewon: a mid-range Korean restaurant or international option — around ₩18,000–28,000

day_by_day.notes: War Memorial of Korea is free and closed on Mondays (check schedule). Leeum Museum entry is around ₩10,000. Itaewon is very international and English-friendly. The area has recovered well and is worth visiting for its unique multicultural character.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park for a winter hike. Take the subway to Gupabal or Dobongsan station. Choose a beginner-friendly trail like the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail. The park is beautiful in winter with snow-dusted peaks and crisp air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the hike and head to Gangnam district — Seoul's upscale southern neighborhood. Visit COEX Mall (one of Asia's largest underground malls) and the famous COEX Starfield Library — a stunning public library inside the mall that's a popular photo spot.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gangnam's Apgujeong Rodeo Street — the heart of Korean celebrity culture, luxury brands, and K-beauty clinics. Window shop and people-watch before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or packed snacks for the hike
meals.lunch: Post-hike meal near the park: doenjang jjigae or sundubu jjigae at a local restaurant — around ₩10,000–15,000
meals.dinner: Gangnam area: upscale Korean BBQ or a trendy restaurant — around ₩25,000–35,000

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan hike requires proper winter hiking shoes with grip — paths can be icy in December. Bring crampons (available for rent near the park entrance). COEX Starfield Library is free to visit. Gangnam is pricier than other areas — budget accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. Beautifully decorated for the winter season (often with lanterns). Explore the temple grounds and learn about Korean Buddhist culture. Nearby Insadong is great for morning browsing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream — a restored urban stream running through central Seoul. Walk along the illuminated stream path (especially magical during the Seoul Lantern Festival season). Visit nearby Gwanghwamun Square and the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration! Head to Myeongdong or Hongdae for the festive atmosphere — streets are decorated, carolers perform, and the city feels magical. Many couples and families celebrate outdoors. Enjoy a special Christmas Eve dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a cozy café near Bupyeong
meals.lunch: Insadong or Cheonggyecheon area: traditional Korean lunch set — around ₩12,000–18,000
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special: a mid-range restaurant in Myeongdong or Hongdae — Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek) is a popular Korean Christmas tradition! — around ₩20,000–30,000

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the busiest nights in Seoul — book dinner reservations in advance. Myeongdong Cathedral holds Christmas Eve Mass (beautiful to observe even for non-Christians). Expect large crowds in popular areas. Dress very warmly for outdoor celebrations.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea. Visit Lotte World — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks, with a K-culture twist. Enjoy rides, ice skating, and the festive Christmas decorations. The park is in Jamsil, easily accessible by subway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at Lotte World or visit the adjacent Lotte World Tower (123 floors — one of the world's tallest buildings). The Seoul Sky observation deck offers breathtaking 360-degree views of Seoul. Nearby Seokchon Lake is beautifully decorated in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jamsil's Rodeo Street or return to a favorite neighborhood for a relaxed Christmas dinner. Many restaurants offer special Christmas menus.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — treat yourself on Christmas morning
meals.lunch: Lotte World food court or a restaurant inside the complex — around ₩12,000–18,000
meals.dinner: Jamsil area: a mid-range Korean or international restaurant with a Christmas special menu — around ₩25,000–35,000

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World entry is around ₩55,000 for adults (all-day pass). Seoul Sky observation deck is around ₩27,000. Christmas Day can be very crowded at Lotte World — arrive early. Many smaller local restaurants may be closed on Christmas Day — plan ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning 5,000 years of history. Entry is free for the permanent collection. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a trendy neighborhood of restored hanok houses converted into cafes, boutiques, and restaurants. More intimate than Bukchon, this area is beloved by young Koreans and perfect for K-culture photography and café hopping.
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening in Seoul — head to a rooftop bar or a special restaurant for a memorable dinner. Consider visiting the Han River (Hangang Park) for a night view of the city lights reflecting on the river, a quintessential Seoul experience.

meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong: a trendy café lunch or Korean fusion restaurant — around ₩12,000–18,000
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner: upscale Korean BBQ (chadolbaegi — beef brisket) or a traditional Korean restaurant — around ₩25,000–40,000

day_by_day.notes: National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays. Ikseon-dong is very photogenic — great for Instagram and K-culture content. Han River parks have convenience stores and food trucks even in winter. Dress extremely warmly for the riverside — wind chill is significant.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast near the hotel. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Bupyeong Modoo Mall or a nearby market. Pack and prepare for departure. Pick up Korean snacks, instant ramyeon, and K-beauty products as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, visit any missed spots near Incheon or head to the airport early. Incheon Airport has excellent duty-free shopping, Korean restaurants, and cultural exhibits inside the terminal. Enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on an incredible 13-day journey through Korean culture, food, history, and K-culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final Korean breakfast: haejang-guk (hangover soup) or congee (juk) at a local restaurant — around ₩8,000–12,000
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant: a final bowl of bibimbap or Korean set meal — around ₩12,000–18,000
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure at Incheon Airport. The AREX train from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport takes about 43 minutes (express) or 66 minutes (all-stop). Duty-free shopping at the airport is excellent — save some budget for last-minute purchases. Tax refund (VAT refund) can be processed at the airport for eligible purchases made during the trip.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon-era royal palace while dressed in traditional Hanbok attire. Hanbok rental shops are located just outside the palace gates, making it easy to combine both activities. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry. Ideal for Day 2 or 3 after settling in, and best done in the morning to avoid crowds. Stay nearby in Jongno-gu to walk directly to the palace.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). The market is lively and authentic, offering a true local food experience without tourist markup. Book a guided food tour or explore independently. Stay in Jongno-gu or Euljiro for easy access.

experiences.name: Hongdae K-Culture & Street Performance Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-pop and youth culture hub. Hongdae is packed with indie music venues, K-pop dance studios offering drop-in classes, street performers, quirky cafes, and K-beauty shops. Join a K-pop dance class at a local studio for around $15–20, then explore the nightlife and street art. This area is best experienced in the late afternoon through evening when energy peaks.

experiences.name: Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Experience
experiences.description: Wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Visit Ssamziegil, an artsy courtyard mall with local designers and handmade goods. Stop at a traditional Korean tea house to try omija tea or sikhye. This culturally rich neighborhood is walkable from Gyeongbokgung and Gwangjang Market, making it perfect for a combined day out. Ideal for mid-trip exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.evening: Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and take the AREX Express Train or private airport transfer to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Light late-night snack near the hotel if hungry.

meals.lunch: In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snack or 24-hour Korean ramen shop near Bupyeong station (try Bupyeong Rodeo Street area for late-night eats)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30 KST. Allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and transfer. Bupyeong is approximately 30–40 minutes from Incheon Airport via AREX + subway. Pre-arrange a private transfer for a premium, stress-free arrival. Rest well — big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast, then explore Bupyeong Modoo Mall and the underground Bupyeong Market — one of Korea's largest underground shopping complexes. Browse local fashion, accessories, and street snacks to ease into Korean culture at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Incheon's Chinatown and Sinpo International Market. Stroll through colorful murals, visit the Jajangmyeon Museum (birthplace of Korean black bean noodles), and explore the nearby Open Port area with its historic Japanese and Chinese concession architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Songdo International Business District (30 min from Bupyeong) for a premium dinner with skyline views. Walk along Songdo Central Park, a stunning urban waterway park illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try a Korean-style breakfast with doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) and rice at a local restaurant
meals.lunch: Sinpo Market's famous Sinpo Dakgangjeong (sweet crispy fried chicken) — a local Incheon specialty since the 1970s
meals.dinner: Hanilkwan Songdo or a premium Korean BBQ restaurant in Songdo — enjoy premium Hanwoo beef (Korean wagyu) with banchan side dishes

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle orientation day to recover from jet lag. Bupyeong and Incheon offer excellent local culture without the crowds of central Seoul. Dress warmly — temperatures around 3°C. Layering is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to central Seoul via subway (Bupyeong to Gyeongbokgung, approx. 60–70 min). Begin the **Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental** experience — rent a stunning traditional Hanbok at one of the premium rental shops near the palace gates (Hanboknam or Gyeongbokgung Hanbok recommended). Explore the grand Joseon-era palace grounds, including Geunjeongjeon Throne Hall and Gyeonghoeru Pavilion, beautifully frosted in winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the adjacent **National Folk Museum of Korea** (free entry with palace ticket) to deepen your understanding of Korean history and traditions. Then stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village — a preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean wooden houses (hanok) with stunning views over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong for the **Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Experience** — browse artisan craft shops, visit Ssamziegil courtyard, and warm up in a traditional tea house with yuja-cha (citron tea) or omija-cha (five-flavor berry tea).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a warm hotteok (sweet pancake) from a street vendor near Bupyeong station before departing
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang near Gyeongbokgung — a legendary restaurant serving premium ginseng chicken soup, perfect for cold winter days (expect a short queue)
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul in Insadong area or Mingles (Michelin-starred modern Korean cuisine) — book in advance for a refined hansik (Korean cuisine) tasting menu experience

day_by_day.notes: Hanbok rental typically costs 20,000–50,000 KRW for 2–3 hours. Wearing Hanbok grants free entry to Gyeongbokgung Palace. Winter palace visits are magical with minimal crowds. Bring hand warmers — it will be cold.

day_by_day.morning: Visit **Changdeokgung Palace** and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) — a serene, forested royal garden that is breathtaking in winter with bare trees and frost. Guided tours of the Secret Garden run at set times; book in advance online.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore **Changgyeonggung Palace** and walk through the connected **Jongmyo Shrine** — a solemn Confucian royal ancestral shrine and UNESCO World Heritage Site. The quiet, minimalist architecture is profoundly moving in winter stillness.
day_by_day.evening: Head to **Cheonggyecheon Stream** for a romantic evening walk along the illuminated urban waterway. Then explore the upscale **Gwanghwamun Square** area, visiting the statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Café Bora in Insadong or Ikseon-dong — famous for its purple taro soft-serve and Korean-style pastries
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market area — premium kimbap, bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), and mayak gimbap at a sit-down restaurant near the market
meals.dinner: Balwoo Gongyang — a Michelin-recommended temple food restaurant near Jogyesa Temple, offering a serene, plant-based Korean Buddhist cuisine experience

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours are limited in winter — book tickets on the Cultural Heritage Administration website at least a week in advance. Jongmyo Shrine is only open on weekends for independent visits; weekday visits require a guided tour.

day_by_day.morning: Full **Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour** — arrive early (9–10am) to experience the market at its most vibrant. Sample bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, yukhoe (Korean beef tartare), and freshly made tteok (rice cakes). Engage with the haenyeo-style grandmothers who have run their stalls for decades.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby **Ikseon-dong Hanok Village** — a trendy neighborhood of converted hanok buildings housing independent cafés, vintage shops, and artisan studios. Perfect for K-culture exploration and unique souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to **Myeongdong** for premium shopping and street food. Visit the flagship stores of Korean beauty brands (Sulwhasoo, History of Whoo, Amorepacific) for luxury K-beauty products. Experience the festive winter street food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel before heading out early
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market — sit at a pojangmacha (covered stall) for an authentic market lunch experience with makgeolli (Korean rice wine)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja — legendary hand-made kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings), a Seoul institution since 1966, or upgrade to Namsangol Hanok Village's premium Korean set dinner

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is busiest on weekends — arrive before 10am to avoid peak crowds. Ikseon-dong is extremely photogenic and perfect for K-culture content. Myeongdong is very crowded on Saturday evenings but the energy is electric.

day_by_day.morning: Visit **N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower)** — take the cable car up Namsan Mountain for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Explore the observation deck and the famous love lock fence. The crisp winter air makes for exceptional visibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore **Namsangol Hanok Village** at the base of Namsan — a beautifully restored traditional village with five authentic hanok houses, a time capsule buried for the Seoul 600th anniversary, and cultural performances on weekends.
day_by_day.evening: Head to **Itaewon** for Seoul's most cosmopolitan dining and nightlife scene. Explore경리단길 (Gyeongnidan-gil) — a charming uphill street lined with independent restaurants, wine bars, and boutique shops.

meals.breakfast: Anthracite Coffee Roasters in Huam-dong (near Namsan) — a stunning café in a converted factory with exceptional specialty coffee and pastries
meals.lunch: Passion 5 Bakery & Café in Hannam-dong — a premium multi-floor patisserie by Paris Croissant with exquisite French-Korean fusion pastries and a full lunch menu
meals.dinner: Vatos Urban Tacos or Cote Korean Steakhouse in Itaewon — premium fusion dining that blends Korean ingredients with international techniques

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower cable car operates from 10am. Weekend Namsangol performances are free. Itaewon is Seoul's most international neighborhood — excellent for those wanting a break from purely Korean cuisine while still experiencing Korean culture through a global lens.

day_by_day.morning: Explore **Gangnam District** — start at the iconic COEX Mall and Starfield Library (a stunning public library inside the mall). Visit the nearby **Bongeunsa Temple**, a 1,200-year-old Buddhist temple dramatically surrounded by Gangnam's skyscrapers — a powerful juxtaposition of ancient and modern Korea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through **Apgujeong Rodeo Street** and **Garosu-gil** (Tree-lined Street) in Sinsa-dong — Seoul's most upscale shopping and café districts. Browse luxury Korean designer boutiques, concept stores, and the flagship stores of global luxury brands.
day_by_day.evening: Experience **K-pop culture** in Gangnam — visit SM Town COEX Artium (SM Entertainment's flagship store and museum), browse K-pop merchandise, and enjoy a premium dinner in the Cheongdam-dong luxury district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium café near Bupyeong before departing
meals.lunch: Garosu-gil café lunch — try Café Bora or Onion Seongsu for artisan sandwiches, salads, and specialty coffee in a beautifully designed space
meals.dinner: Cheongdam-dong fine dining — La Yeon (The Shilla Hotel, 3 Michelin stars) for the ultimate Korean haute cuisine experience, or Jungsik for modern Korean tasting menu. Reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: La Yeon at The Shilla Hotel is one of Asia's finest restaurants — reservations should be made weeks in advance. Bongeunsa Temple offers free lantern-making workshops on some weekdays. Gangnam is about 90 minutes from Bupyeong by subway.

day_by_day.morning: **Hongdae K-Culture & Street Performance Walk** — arrive in Hongdae (Hongik University area) mid-morning when the neighborhood begins to come alive. Explore the vibrant street art, indie music shops, K-pop dance studios, and quirky concept stores. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or LINE Friends flagship store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring **Yeonnam-dong** — Hongdae's quieter, more residential neighbor known as 'Seoul's Brooklyn.' Wander through its charming streets lined with independent cafés, bookshops, and vintage clothing stores. Visit Gyeongui Line Forest Park — a linear park built on a former railway line.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Hongdae's legendary nightlife — live indie music at Club FF or Freebird, or enjoy a premium cocktail bar experience at Charles H. (Four Seasons Hotel) or Alice Cheongdam.

meals.breakfast: Café Onion Anguk or a local bakery near the hotel before heading to Hongdae
meals.lunch: Hongdae's famous street food — try hotteok, tteokbokki, and Korean corn dogs from street vendors, or sit down at Maple Tree House for premium Korean BBQ
meals.dinner: Yeonnam-dong restaurant row — Palsaik Samgyeopsal (8-flavor pork belly BBQ) for a fun, interactive premium Korean BBQ dinner experience

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae street performances are most active on weekends but some buskers perform on weekdays too. The area is extremely popular with young Koreans and international tourists — great for K-culture immersion. Many shops open late (noon–10pm).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to **Suwon Hwaseong Fortress** (1 hour from Seoul/Bupyeong by subway) — a magnificent UNESCO World Heritage fortress wall built in 1796 during the Joseon Dynasty. Walk the full 5.7km fortress wall circuit for stunning winter views over the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore **Suwon's Haenggung Palace** (the temporary royal palace within the fortress) and the traditional **Paldalmun Market** — one of Korea's most authentic traditional markets, famous for Suwon galbi (grilled short ribs).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul/Incheon area. Stop in **Yeouido** on the way back — Seoul's financial district and home to the IFC Mall. Enjoy the winter Han River Park views and the festive Christmas decorations along the riverbank.

meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (grilled beef short ribs) at Yeongdong Galbi or Hwaseong Sikdang near the fortress — Suwon is the birthplace of this iconic Korean dish
meals.dinner: Yeouido IFC Mall dining — The Lounge at Conrad Seoul for premium afternoon tea turned dinner, or Balwoo Gongyang for a refined Korean meal

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is easily accessible from Bupyeong via subway (1 transfer). The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Dress in very warm layers — walking the exposed fortress walls in December wind is cold but spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Visit **Lotte World** in Jamsil — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks, or explore the adjacent **Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory** (555m tall, 5th tallest building in the world) for breathtaking panoramic views of Seoul on a clear winter day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore **Seokchon Lake** surrounding Lotte World — beautifully decorated for Christmas with elaborate light installations. Visit **Songpa Naru Park** and the nearby **Olympic Park** (built for the 1988 Seoul Olympics) with its outdoor sculpture garden.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul — experience the festive atmosphere in **Myeongdong** or **Cheongdam-dong**, both elaborately decorated for Christmas. Seoul has a vibrant Christmas culture; enjoy the lights, carol performances, and festive street food.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel breakfast or Tartine Bakery Seoul for French-style pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Jamsil area — Lotte World Food Court for a variety of Korean dishes, or Maple Tree House Jamsil for premium Korean BBQ with Lotte Tower views
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — The Dining Room at Park Hyatt Seoul or Nobu Seoul for a premium festive dining experience. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of Seoul's biggest celebration nights — the city transforms with lights and festivities. Myeongdong Cathedral holds a midnight mass that is open to all visitors. Book Christmas Eve dinner reservations at least 2 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Peaceful Christmas morning — visit **Jogyesa Temple** in central Seoul, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with colorful lanterns year-round. Attend a morning ceremony for a deeply cultural experience. Then walk through the quiet, festive streets of **Insadong**.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the **National Museum of Korea** in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an extraordinary collection of Korean art, history, and artifacts spanning 5,000 years. The museum is free and world-class.
day_by_day.evening: Visit **Hangang Park** (Han River Park) for a winter evening stroll. The river views with city lights reflecting on the water are magical on Christmas night. Warm up with a cup of hot chocolate from a riverside café.

meals.breakfast: Slow Christmas morning breakfast at a premium café — try Fritz Coffee Company in Mapo for exceptional specialty coffee and croissants
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea's Café ON:THE TABLE for a refined Korean lunch with museum garden views
meals.dinner: Premium Christmas dinner — Gaon (3 Michelin stars, Gangnam) for the pinnacle of Korean fine dining, or Kwon Sooksoo for an intimate, chef-driven Korean tasting menu. Reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea — most attractions are open but some smaller shops may be closed. The National Museum of Korea is free entry and one of Seoul's most underrated premium experiences. Gaon is considered one of the best restaurants in Asia.

day_by_day.morning: Explore **Seongsu-dong** — Seoul's trendiest emerging neighborhood, often called 'Seoul's Brooklyn.' Visit artisan coffee roasters, concept stores in converted factories, and the famous **Daelim Warehouse** cultural space. Browse the weekend flea market if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Han River to **Bukhansan National Park** for a gentle winter hike — the park is within Seoul city limits and offers stunning granite peaks and Buddhist temples. The Bukhansanseong Fortress trail offers accessible winter hiking with spectacular views.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium shopping evening in **Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)** — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic building hosts design exhibitions, fashion shows, and a massive shopping complex. The building is dramatically lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Seongsu-dong specialty coffee — Daelim Changgo or Café Onion Seongsu (a converted factory café, one of Seoul's most Instagrammed spaces) for artisan coffee and Korean-style brunch
meals.lunch: Seongsu-dong's trendy restaurant row — try Seongsudong Sutbul Galbi for premium charcoal-grilled Korean beef in an industrial-chic setting
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — Gwangjang Market for a final evening of authentic Korean street food, or upgrade to a premium Korean seafood restaurant in the area for haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) and fresh raw fish

day_by_day.notes: Seongsu-dong is best explored on foot — the neighborhood is compact and walkable. Bukhansan hike requires proper winter hiking shoes and warm layers. DDP is open until late and the night architecture is extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — revisit a favorite neighborhood or experience you want to savor one last time. Consider a final visit to **Gyeongbokgung Palace** at opening time (9am) for a quiet, uncrowded farewell to the palace in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Toyoko Inn Bupyeong, check out, and collect luggage. Final Korean lunch near Bupyeong before heading to Incheon Airport. Allow 3 hours before departure for international flights. Browse duty-free shops at Incheon Airport — one of the world's best airport shopping experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Incheon Airport's duty-free offers premium Korean products: red ginseng, Korean cosmetics (Sulwhasoo, Whoo), Korean snacks, and traditional crafts — perfect for last-minute premium gifts.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) and rice at a local restaurant near Gyeongbokgung, or a premium hotel breakfast if time allows
meals.lunch: Bupyeong area farewell lunch — try a local Korean restaurant for doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) or galbitang (short rib soup) — comforting, warming Korean classics
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport — Korean Air Lounge or a premium airport restaurant. Try Bibigo at the airport for a final taste of Korean cuisine before departure

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 11am — arrange late check-out if needed (may incur extra charge). Incheon Airport is 30–40 minutes from Bupyeong via AREX. Allow extra time on Sunday due to potential weekend crowds. Incheon Airport's Terminal 1 and 2 both have excellent duty-free and dining options.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX
